walkthroughs.body_html:
The big one: v = f × λ.

Wave speed (m/s) equals frequency (Hz) times wavelength (m). Multiply the two and you get the speed.

Quick example: a wave with f = 4 Hz and λ = 3 m has speed v = 4 × 3 = 12 m/s. Easy. 👍

Need frequency? Use f = v ÷ λ. Need wavelength? Use λ = v ÷ f.

Same triangle trick as speed-distance-time: cover the one you want, divide or multiply the others.

Always check the units match before plugging in: speed in m/s, wavelength in m, frequency in Hz.

The period T is how long one wave takes — measured in seconds. It's linked to frequency by T = 1 / f.

A 5 Hz wave has T = 1/5 = 0.2 s per wave.

Wave speed also depends on the medium. Sound travels faster in water than in air. Light slows down inside glass. The medium matters!

options: λ = v × f
λ = v / f
λ = f / v
λ = v + f

options: 2 s
5 s

mcqs.q: When a wave travels through water, what happens to the water itself?
options: The water oscillates about a fixed point; the wave transfers energy, not matter.
The water turns into wave material and changes state.
The water moves along with the wave from one place to another.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.

mcqs.q: What property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
options: The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
Amplitude determines pitch — a bigger wave is a higher-pitched note.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.
The frequency — higher frequency means higher pitch.

mcqs.q: How do you see a non-luminous object like a book?
options: Light from a source reflects off the book and enters your eyes.
Your eyes send out beams of vision that hit the book and let you see it.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.
